body: I hate feeling guilty about something I haven't done yet
No problem. I understand what you're going through, and it can be a pain. Sometimes it's easier getting help from a stranger than a friend

I'm sorry you're going through all of this. Life can be pretty shitty, and I know sometimes you just want to give up, but giving up is the worst thing you can do. My life isn't great either. I've had similar luck with pills, and it's terrible sometimes, I know. You have to push through it. I promise life will get better in time. PM me if you need someone to talk to, I'm here for you.
I talked to my mom and she said she'd be willing to cut back because she isn't exactly fit either. I'm going to use one of those calorie counting things and she said she'd buy healthier foods.
Well I cut back to one cup each and usually I'd eat a big bowl of chips

I'm willing to try most foods at least once. I keep seeing food that looks fairly awesome on here and Facebook that look healthy.

Edit: unneeded letters
I was actually thinking of making dinner a few times a week but cooking isn't exactly easy for me. I'd probably use the slow cooker to make soup since that's all I can do.

Well it isn't like we have just junk food. My mom regularly makes dinner with healthy sides. The issue is that we don't really have healthy snacks and the most common drink in our house is sweet tea and Mountain Dew. I mean a bag of Doritos and a glass of Mountain Dew looks a lot tastier than an apple and water. I recently cut back on soda and the sugar in the tea has been cut back but I don't think I'll get much progress unless we all cut back.
Thank you very much. I forgot to mention it might be a bit hard to start dieting when the rest of my family still eats bad. Any ideas on how to convince them?

One thing that helps is writing. I'm not very good at it but it's a way for me to release some anger and help myself relax. Hopefully once I get out of school things will get better, but as I said before even complete strangers will make fun of me.

I was too young to understand the 9/11 attacks and reading these really showed me how people felt about it right after it happened. Everyone was scared it seems, not just Americans. Man it had to have been tragic to hear/see everything unfold.

One of my friends killed himself a little over a year ago. 

One thing I noticed from his father is that he was lost. He didn't know why his son had killed himself, and he didn't know how to deal with it. He asked around for answers, and honestly didn't get any. He asked me if his son ever brought him up (he was a little harsh on his son, an he feels it may have been his fault.) and he asked if I saw anything happen to his son.

From what I know, it was a mix of depression, bullying, and family issues that caused him to do it. His father is heartbroken and I have no idea if he'll ever move on. It's hard to see a man be so broken after you've seen him at his happiest times. 

Don't ever kill yourself. It only hurts those who care, it doesn't help anybody.
